There's no way around it from inside the session: the guard refuses any command containing `eval`, and your own `!` command is refused the same way. A wrapper script, alias or another tool doesn't get past it either. Paste this into a terminal outside Claude Code:

```bash
claude plugin eval /srv/work/notes-wt/plugins/notes --json /srv/work/notes-wt/out.json
```

Don't try to bypass it; wrapping it in PowerShell or a script won't help. Run it in a separate terminal:

`claude plugin eval ~/work/notes-wt/plugins/notes --json ~/work/notes-wt/out.json`

Then ask the session to read out.json.

No workaround. Open a regular terminal and run:

```bash
claude plugin eval <absolute-worktree-path>/plugins/notes --json <absolute-worktree-path>/out.json
```
